title: An Egg Holds 3 kg, So How Does a Chick Get Out? 🐣
description:
Why doesn't an egg crack when a hen sits on it? The egg's dome shape spreads outside pressure across the whole shell, so an egg squeezed end to end can hold about 3 kg, while a chick pecking one spot from the inside, and pulling calcium from the shell as it grows, breaks out easily.

Sources:
https://www.scienceworld.ca/resource/unsqueezable-egg/
https://scienceinsights.org/how-much-force-does-it-take-to-break-an-egg/

topic: Why doesn't an egg crack when a hen sits on it?
script:
A hen sits on her eggs for 21 days,
and they don't crack.
So how does a tiny chick break out?
It's all about the shape.
An egg is a dome, like a stone arch.
Push on the outside,
and the force spreads across the whole shell,
so no single spot takes the load.
Squeezed end to end,
an egg can hold about three kilos.
Plus the hen's weight is shared by the nest and the other eggs.
From the inside, it's a different story.
The chick pecks one tiny spot,
and a dome is weak against a push from inside.
Here's the clever part.
The chick pulls calcium from the shell to build its bones,
so the shell gets thinner as it grows.
Strong outside, weak inside.
So could you crack an egg squeezing it end to end?
key_facts: A chicken egg takes about 21 days to hatch
The dome/arch shape spreads an outside load across the whole shell
A fresh egg pressed evenly takes roughly 30-40 N (about 3-4 kg) to break
A hen's weight is spread over the nest and the clutch
Pressure from inside on one spot is the shell's weak direction
During incubation the embryo draws calcium from the shell's inner layers, thinning it
